audience: a parent or patient-group leader without medical training

sentences.text: Constellate computed a weak symptom similarity between glycogen storage disease II and Sandhoff disease, with a score of 0.166 over 8 shared terms, ranked 4 of 26 [e_ea2d0ba2a4af].
This link is inferred, meaning Constellate calculated it, and it is not a database finding [e_ea2d0ba2a4af].

The causes differ: glycogen storage disease II is linked to the gene GAA, but only by an inferred roll-up from subtypes at confidence 0.475, while Sandhoff disease is curated as caused by HEXB [e_98d3f35813c2] [e_64451e791aad].
Sandhoff disease has two studies not yet recruiting on ClinicalTrials.gov, one of gene therapy using blood samples and one of a drug called PLX-200 in children [e_3970483dad5d] [e_b9be2fdad34e].
Two patient groups are linked to it, one by an automatic name match and one by a text-mined link that is unverified [e_18880301ed7f] [e_6444d735654b].
A research grant on mouse models of sphingolipid biology is also recorded [e_89596e9236d9].
For glycogen storage disease II, curated records list low acid maltase activity and progressive muscle weakness, both very frequent [e_8010ab0e798a] [e_ad2b0bfab1c5].
These edges do not show a shared cause or that the Sandhoff studies apply to glycogen storage disease II [e_ea2d0ba2a4af] [e_3970483dad5d].
